headline: Council authorizes lawsuit settlement, approves Aloha Classic permit, refers rezoning to committee

meeting.voteItem: Motion to discharge Resolution 26-128 from committee
meeting.summary: The council voted to authorize settling a suit by the Conservation Council of Hawaiʻi and American Bird Conservancy and approved a Hoʻokipa permit for the 2026 Aloha Classic. Six-parcel rezoning and Bill 102 on parking went to the Water and Infrastructure Committee.
meeting.recap: Eight council members were present, and one was excused.[[0:02:54]] The budget director said the Board of Ethics' half-time investigator needs to be full-time.[[0:19:09]] The council voted to authorize settling a lawsuit brought by the Conservation Council of Hawaiʻi and the American Bird Conservancy.[[0:45:57]] The settlement terms were discussed in executive session (a closed-door discussion).[[0:46:05]] The council approved a permit for the 2026 Aloha Classic windsurfing tournament at Hoʻokipa Beach Park.[[0:49:32]] The council accepted a $1,000 donation for a lauhala (pandanus leaf) weaving workshop for county employees.[[0:51:20]] A rezoning request for six parcels, including Maui Ocean Center, was sent to the Water and Infrastructure Committee.[[0:52:04]] The council approved moving $42,546 within the Board of Ethics budget.[[0:53:05]] Bill 103 would extend a property tax exemption for wildfire-impacted properties to June 30, 2028.[[0:59:28]] Bill 107 would add a $390,038 state health grant for kūpuna (elder) care services.[[1:01:32]] Bill 95 expands the county's fare-free bus pass program.[[1:02:15]]
decided: The council voted to pull Resolution 26-128 out of committee so it could act on it at this meeting.
The council adopted the resolution allowing a special events permit for the 2026 Aloha Classic windsurfing tournament.
The resolution on rezoning six parcels was referred to the Water and Infrastructure Committee with no objections.
The council adopted the resolution moving $42,546 within the Board of Ethics program.
Bill 102, about stopping, standing, parking and loading zones, was referred to the Water and Infrastructure Committee with no objections.
meeting.next: The budget director said she will confirm whether the County owns Hale Aloha and report back. A council member asked the department to share the lauhala workshop dates so the council can spread the word.

issues.why: The budget director said Bill 103 updates the exemption's end date to line up with Ordinance 5913.

deadlines.t: New expiration date for the real property tax exemption for wildfire-impacted properties.

issues.brief: The exemption's end date would change from December 31, 2026 to June 30, 2028.[[#1]] Bill 106 would add Hale Aloha to the properties covered by Lahaina Restoration Foundation funds.[[#2]] Hale Aloha had been left out of that budget condition by mistake.[[#3]]
